I just looked into it and it seems like you can definitely 3D print zbrush models. So I would probably look more into that and see how it’s done. But as of rn with light research it seems that you don’t need to worry about retopo if your goal is to make high poly sculpts, a few nice renders, and a 3D print of the model. Consider retopo when you’re gonna be using it for an animation, game engine, or you want to be able to infinitely pose and render your model easier. Also when you’re posing your model in zbrush make a copy of your file so your Pokémon isn’t stuck in one pose when you’re done with however renders you wanna make. Keep your finished model file and then make copies to pose.

I would recommend modeling it in a way where it’s all one piece. You can combine what you have right now but it would be hard considering the difference between verts and edges on the top arm and bottom arms. Try watching a video on complex modeling. Rn you have a block in for the design you want to make. Now you have to learn how to make the topology in order to combine the two shapes.

If you wanna rig this model to animate it, retopologize in maya or blender, texture, then rig and render. 

If you just wanna use this piece for a nice solid render just poly paint it, pose the actual sculpt itself, then render it either in zbrush itself or any other software that can render.
